method_note: Review tiers are paused (tiers paused, research only) since 2026-11-03: no tier, colour, grade or tier count is published, and each row's probabilities are research only. One row per institution with a fresh vetted public dossier (nothing older than 183 days for quarterly filings or 400 days for annual filings is presented as current; failed institutions are replayed on the Evidence tab instead). Components are replayed independently on the 48-institution construction-PIT record and fused only for presentation — the tier is a published rule over published components. PD levels are corpus-fitted and prior-corrected to a ~0.25%/yr population base rate (King-Zeng); the Merton PD is a market repricing signal, not a calibrated failure frequency. Stale, future-dated, or unclocked market readings remain visible but have no signal or tier authority. The conformal alarm is retained as a diagnostic, but its historical tier wiring is suspended and it has no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation. Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design: nothing here is scored from memory. Newer accepted bank filing reviews are returned separately as current_disclosures; they do not inherit historical model scores or enter the training corpus. Corpus cohort labels such as healthy_control describe historical calibration membership.

tier_publication.label: tiers paused, research only
tier_publication.reason: Re-dating three co-operative bank failures to their onset removed a mis-dated training event from the hazard panel. The refit model's out-of-time discrimination fell (current figures at /api/failure-radar/validation) and the refit alone would move institutions between tiers. Tiers stay unpublished until the model re-validates.
